key_evidence: On 2026-09-11 a federal jury in the Northern District of Oklahoma found Progressive breached its duty of good faith and fair dealing in handling Mary Paulding’s underinsured-motorist claim, awarding $20 million compensatory and $20 million punitive damages. A jury verdict on the merits is a tier-5 adjudicated finding, not an allegation.

The claim was for $25,000 in underinsured-motorist benefits after an August 2022 crash. Plaintiff counsel states Progressive’s response was an offer of $710. The court found the investigation was unnecessarily delayed and that Progressive demanded records it either already possessed or did not need.

Trial evidence accepted by the court: adjusters "lacked a basic understanding of how to handle Oklahoma underinsured motorist claims" and were incentivised through a company-wide profit share program to reduce loss payouts and claim costs. This is a structural finding, not a single-adjuster error.

Appeal status: Progressive is seeking post-verdict relief in Tulsa federal court and an appeal is expected. The judgment is NOT final, which is why AB5 Reparative Action scores at the floor rather than being credited.

Countervailing and genuinely strong: Progressive ranked #19 on Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For 2026 (ninth consecutive year, highest-ranked insurer) and #1 on Forbes America’s Best Employers for Company Culture 2026 from 217,000 worker responses. B1 holds at 4/5 and I3 at 4/5 on that independent evidence.

The published 76.3 is an unassessed placeholder (six dimensions at exactly 4.0, last_assessed null). It reconstructs canonically as 70.3 base plus a 6.0 integration premium, so any evidence-based move below 4.0 removes the premium as well as lowering the base.

notes: Two-band crossing (Established to Developing) on a -39.4 delta. The magnitude requires reviewer scrutiny and is disclosed honestly: the tier-5 verdict drives Accountability to 1.8 and Action/Empathy to 2.4, but a large share of the total movement is de-seeding - the published 4.0s asserted anchor-4 behaviour for which no evidence was located, and the methodology requires the lower anchor when evidence is absent. Peer calibration supports the result: among insurers already assessed with evidence, State Farm sits at 13.8, Cigna 20.3, Centene 32.8 and Humana 35.2, so Progressive at 36.9 sits above all of them. Calibration flag recorded separately and NOT used to justify this move: Allstate (48.4), The Hartford, Travelers, MetLife and Unum (all 60.9) and Aflac (92.4) sit on unassessed uniform plateaus in the same sector and warrant band-wide review. Watch trigger: a successful appeal would be material to AB1, AB5 and I4 and should force reassessment.
